newsitem.title: RUSSIA: China minister rules out alliance with Moscow.
newsitem.headline: China minister rules out alliance with Moscow.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen on Thursday ruled out China's entering into any kind of alliance with Russia, even as it builds a "strategic partnership" with Moscow.

Qian also made clear that the declaration of opposition to the world hegemony of one state -- a clear reference to the United States -- in a Sino-Russian declaration signed on Wednesday would not sour Beijing's relations with Washington.
"There can be no word about any kind of alliance," Qian told a news conference held after the end of the official part of Chinese President Jiang Zemin's state visit to Moscow.
"We have tried alliance and we have tried confrontation," Qian said, referring to the Soviet-Chinese alliance of 1950s which later collapsed into more than two decades of hostility.
"Both did not work and now we must find something else," Qian added. "Our relations are not confrontational but they are not an alliance either."
Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Jiang confirmed during the visit that they are committed to building "partnership aimed at strategic co-operation in the 21st century".

They signed a political declaration condemning claims by any country of a leading role in the post-Cold War world. The declaration did not contain any reference to a specific country but there was little doubt that it referred to Washington.
"I would not want to focus on the object of that clause," said Qian, who goes to Washington later in April.
"We said that we favour a multi-polar world expressing the idea we share with Russia," Qian said. "Others may have different views."
